reviews.summary:
Verdict: do not show it to the owner as it is. It is about a day of fixes away. Figure B (mask stacks) and the timing diagram are ready now; the block-diagram kit and the cost chart are not.

What is good
- B is the best thing here: three isometric stacks only this course could have, and the 0 / 2 / 4 lit layers read in two seconds in both themes.
- The timing diagram reads like a waveform viewer (cyan level on a deepening fill, indigo bus cells on a screen).
- Parts in a state (ok / error, kit-states) stand out properly against the rest.
- The panel, title strip with the tier indicator, and legend chips give every figure one frame. Fuchsia as "what it costs" is a sound hue choice, clear of all protected hues.

What is not
- Richness is spread evenly, so nothing leads. Every ordinary part gets the full gradient, rim and shadow, and the focal part gets only a same-hue glow on top. Testbench figures become a wall of saturated brown, design figures a wall of purple gradient boxes, and the focal part is invisible. Only one of the five kit samples has a focal part at all.
- The cost chart contradicts the lesson's colour story: dimming unselected bars to 60% makes the selected x1 bar more intense than the x10,000 bar. The chart also jumps up to 21 px as stages are clicked.
- A, B and the timing diagrams float in half-empty panels (44 to 65% of the stage width).
- Calm is not a second setting: it differs from rich by 0.7 to 5.3 levels out of 255 on average.
- In tier 4 lessons a part with no role is drawn in the testbench hue family, with no legend chip.
- Lesson 1 is only partly converted: six hand-drawn figures are still bare grey, including the recap strip that A's caption calls "the same strip".
- Light mode is flatter: A's plates are near-white boxes with coloured outlines, B's reused layers are grey, and glows vanish.

Calm against rich: rich should be the default. Calm as built is not worth offering; either redefine it (flat parts, no field, no glow) or drop it.

Not checked from my lens: forced colours, print and reduced motion (I looked only at A in forced colours and print, which were fine).

Scripts, crops and extra captures are in <scratch>/figures/art/review/design/ (measure.cjs, pix.cjs, hue.cjs, jitter.cjs, t4.cjs, cap.cjs, crops.cjs, b.cjs). Nothing in the repository was edited.

Teaching review of the figure art-direction preview (worktree commit 1102f758 against live cb80965f). I would not show it to the owner as it is: figures A and B are ready, chart C needs a small fix, and the kit-wide change has one S1 and one S2 that should be fixed first.

**What is good**
- **Words and numbers:** every string in A and B is unchanged against cb80965f (29 of 29 and 37 of 37 strings, same sizes and weights), and the rest of the lesson is byte-identical.
- **Chart C behaviour:** 25 states operated on both servers (unanswered, each of the four predictions, reveal, five stages in cost and delay views, three anchors, slider keys) gave byte-identical text, aria values, bar geometry and delay widths.
- **Figure A:** the tape-out line as the focal part matches the lesson's own sentence ("the line that changes what a fix means"). The two wells show which fix belongs to which side better than the old brackets did. The line is still dashed, between the third and fourth plates, and the arrow still points right under the row.
- **Figure B:** every statement in the desc and caption still holds. Each stack has three metal slabs over one base; (a) is all dashed, (b) has the two upper slabs hatched and the lowest metal and base solid, (c) is all hatched. The via runs from the lower new slab through the reused metal to the spare cell on the base. The 0, 2, 4 count of lit layers reads at a glance, and forced colours keep hatched, solid and dashed apart.
- **Kit states and signals:** ok and error states, role tags, legends and the timing diagram's protected colours (cyan 1, slate 0, indigo buses) read correctly under the new depth. Cyan still means selected in C.

**What is not**
- **S1, kit:** a part with no role is now painted in the tier hue, which in Tier 3 is the design violet and in Tier 4 the testbench amber. The formal tool in a Tier 4 figure now looks like a testbench part.
- **S2, chart C:** dimming unselected bars to 60% breaks the ramp order. The selected bar looks "more" than the next stage in 4 of 5 selections, including the default view.
- **S2, kit focal:** of 27 automatic focal picks across 157 figures in 21 lessons, 14 are right, 7 point at the wrong part and 6 are arbitrary.
- **S2, lesson 1:** the un-redrawn decisions figure says it uses "the encoding of the respin figure" and "the respin figure's reused fill", which is no longer true; B's unchanged desc and lead-in still say "cross-sections".
- **S3:** five smaller points, listed below.

**Suggested order**
1. Make no-role parts neutral again.
2. Keep all bars in C at full ramp fill.
3. Replace the automatic focal with an authored one.
4. Redraw the decisions and recap figures before the lesson is shown whole.

Everything is in <scratch>/figures/art/review/teaching/ (scripts, JSON captures and screenshots).

Robustness review of the figure art direction preview (worktree commit 1102f758, compared with the live site on port 3000). Nothing is broken and no test fails, but six measured problems should be fixed before the owner sees it; I would not show it exactly as it is.

**What is good**
- **Tests:** the 8 named and kit test files pass (554 tests), 33 further test files for components that embed kit figures pass (486 tests), `tsc --noEmit` is clean, and `check-mdx --render` is clean on lesson 1 and four other lessons.
- **Site-wide sweep:** 126 kit figures in 8 lessons across the four tiers, dark and light, show no new text overlap, no legend or title overflow, no figure breaking a `<details>` or an interactive, no page-level sideways scroll at 390, and no console error.
- **Contrast in A, B and C at desktop:** every label holds 4.5:1 in rich and calm, dark and light (lowest 7.04 inside the drawings, 10.06 on a title strip). Marks hold 3:1 (lowest 3.63), apart from the delay bars below.
- **Kit figures:** legend swatches are at least 4.75:1, title indicators at least 4.91:1, and tags at least 4.83:1.
- **Forced colours and print:** text is 21:1 in forced colours, light and dark. B keeps hatched, plain-outlined and dashed plates apart. Print with a dark preference uses the light values and reads well.
- **Reduced motion:** nothing in a kit figure moves, and C's bar and button transitions switch off.
- **C's height:** unchanged in all three bands.
- **Cost:** no clear slowdown on a 26-figure lesson (B-AMBA-F3, dev servers, medians of three runs). First paint to idle was 1035 ms against 1071 ms, main-thread task time 744 against 733 ms, and no scroll step exceeded 50 ms on either. The page gains 14% more DOM nodes, 52 filters and 71 gradients.

**What is not good (all S2)**
1. Six interactives that embed kit figures now render 15 to 63 px taller than their reserved heights.
2. In rich dark, port labels that sit on a lit object fall to 3.99:1.
3. In rich light and in print, the high level line of timing diagrams falls to 2.73:1 against its own fill.
4. The 12 px stage padding makes B's labels drop below 11 px on a phone.
5. The same padding makes two figures that used to fit scroll sideways.
6. C's delay view draws the unselected bars at 2.0 to 2.65:1.

**Would I show it as it is?** No. Items 2 to 5 are one- or two-line CSS or class changes, and item 2 is visible in the default rich dark look on every UVM component diagram with ports. Item 1 is a release gate rather than a preview gate, but the owner should be told it is pending.

**Limits of this review**
- The repository's height tool is not in the worktree, whose base predates checkpoint 30. I ran the copy in the main checkout against both servers and compared rendered heights; the raw 3210 run in `heights.json` lists 148 over, mostly from the stale registry.
- Cost was measured on dev servers in headless desktop Chromium, not on a phone.

Evidence is in `<scratch>/figures/art/review/robustness/` (scripts, logs, `out/`); the key numbers are in `measurements.txt` there. "That folder" below means this one.

findings: S2 [design] Kit block diagrams with many testbench parts (self-checking loop, component tree, states), rich and calm, dark, 1440: A wall of saturated brown in which the focal part cannot be found. 7 of 8 parts in the self-checking loop are amber, and the deep amber body turns brown in dark mode. The focal part (compare / SCB) has exactly the same body as an ordinary part; its only difference is an amber glow on an amber outline, and in light mode nothing visible. The eye goes to the one violet DUT, which is not the focal part. The earlier near-neutral fill with a bright amber outline was cleaner.

S2 [design] Kit block diagrams with one role and no focal part (AHB single master; also component tree and the tier 4 phase figure), rich, dark and light, 1440: Six identical purple gradient boxes under a violet title strip with indigo glow lines: no hierarchy, and in dark mode it looks like a generic purple-gradient card layout. The title names "decoder, multiplexor and the HREADY loop" but nothing is distinguished, because the focal rule (most data lines arriving, no tie) finds no part. Of the five kit samples only the self-checking loop has a focal part, so rule 1 of section 14 is not met on most kit figures.

S2 [design] Kit block diagram in a tier 4 lesson (E-CUST-1, "Two domains, and the container each phase lives in"), rich, dark and light, 1440: Parts with no role are drawn in the testbench hue family. The clear-glass tint and tier-mixed rim come from the tier 4 amber, so phase boxes look like muted testbench parts, and there is no legend chip for that colour (rule 4 asks for one). The same mechanism gives violet (design) in tier 3 and teal (expected) in tier 1, where A's tape-out line and B's reused layers are already teal. The dark version is also a second all-brown figure with nothing lit.

S2 [design] C, cost chart in InteractiveCostOfBugGraph, cost and delay views, rich and calm, dark and light, 1440 and 390: The fuchsia ramp is inverted by the selection. Unselected bars drop to 60% fill, so the selected bar is always the most intense. With Spec selected, the x1 bar is brighter (dark) or darker (light) than the x10,000 bar, which says the opposite of "fuchsia is what it costs". The component's own comment says selection is a separate cue and the bar keeps its step. At 60% the steps are also only 1.12 to 1.16:1 apart, so the ramp reads as one dusky mauve.

S2 [design] C, cost chart card, cost view, both themes, 1440: The chart moves up and down as the learner steps through the stages. This commit added justify-center to the chart card, and the card's height follows the readout text beside it, so the chart is re-centred on every selection.

S2 [design] A and B (rich and calm, both themes, 1440) and kit timing diagrams (AHB lesson, 1440): The drawings do not fill their panels. A and B are capped at 520 px in a 798 px stage, leaving 139 px of empty glass each side. Timing screens are 348 to 500 px wide in the same stage. In B the wells hold the stack and layer labels but not the row's heading and text, so half of each row sits on bare stage and the wells group the wrong things.

S2 [design] Calm against rich, all eight visuals, both themes: Calm is not distinct enough to offer. Side by side the two are hard to tell apart, most of all in light mode and in C. The loudest marks (A's wedge arrow, outlines, text) are identical in both; only body alpha, glow and field change.

S2 [design] Lesson 1 page as a whole (F1A), both themes, 1440: The lesson is only partly converted, and the owner will scroll all of it. Six other hand-drawn figures (life, shift, ladder, recap, decisions, sign-off) are still bare grey outlines, left-aligned, with no panel. The recap strip tells the same five-stage story with x1 to x10,000 and a tape-out line in neutral grey, so "one colour story for the lesson" breaks on the same page. A's caption says the recap "draws the same strip", which no longer looks true.

S2 [design] A, rich and calm, dark and light, 1440: The declared focal part is not the loudest thing. The tape-out line is a thin dashed teal line with a small flag. The fuchsia wedge arrow is the largest saturated mass in the figure, at nearly the same luminance, and stops short of meeting the line. Two elements compete and the arrow wins, in calm exactly as in rich.

S2 [design] A and B in light mode (rich), 1440; focal glow in every light figure: Light mode is flatter than dark. A's plates are near-white at the top, so they read as outlined boxes with a faint tint, not objects. B's reused layers and their legend swatch are effectively grey. The focal glow is invisible on the kit figures.

S2 [design] Kit sequence diagram (I-UVM-1A), rich, dark and light, 1440: The promised signature, the lit trace, is grey here. Calls, returns and step badges are all neutral grey on brown rails, so the body of the figure is grey and brown on a strong blue field. Light mode is almost unchanged from before apart from cream headers. The tier 2 blue field and title strip are also much heavier than tier 1's teal on A.

S3 [design] Kit block diagrams, rich, both themes: The 7 px trace band has round caps that poke over a part's outline and into its fill at both ends of every data line, leaving pale blobs on the border and under arrowheads.

S3 [design] C, whole interactive, both themes, 1440 and 390: Three nested frames (figure panel with 24 px padding, amber predict card, chart card) put the chart, the one rich element, at 324x172 px inside an 800 px interactive. The amber frame inside the teal field reads muddy before the reveal. On a phone the three frames take about 80 px of width.

S3 [design] A, rich and calm, both themes, 1440: Small composition faults. The two wells set their text with different leading and padding (left 19 px, two lines centred; right about 17 px, three lines, about 6 px from the well's bottom). The "fix = ..." annotations have the same size, weight and colour as the stage names. Wells, plates and flag all carry a 2 px outline, so the wells read as boxes around boxes, not a recessed tray.

S3 [design] B, rich, dark and light, 1440: Details that still look machine-made. Stack (a) is a tangle of short dashes in which four plates cannot be counted. The spare-cell via is a flat vertical line and square pasted over an isometric drawing. In dark, all four plates of (c) carry the full glow, so (c) becomes a heavy pink mass. The legend is drawn inside the SVG with square swatches, while kit figures use the panel's legend strip of chips.

S3 [design] Panel typography and captions, all figures, both themes: Inconsistent text roles. The title strip is the smallest text in the figure although it names it. Timing and architecture figures set their figcaption inside the panel at 12 px, while sequence figures and the hand-drawn A and B set theirs below the panel at 14 to 15 px.

S3 [design] A and B, rich, dark, 390: The panel makes phone text smaller. The stage padding and border narrow the drawing from 358 to 332 px, so A's labels fall to 9.7 px and B's to 10.3 to 11.7 px. The drawing shrinks; it does not scroll, although section 14 says it scrolls as before.

S3 [design] Kit samples chosen for the preview (self-checking loop, component tree), all settings: Layout collisions that predate this work sit in the middle of the samples and look worse now that the parts are lit: the REF tag runs under step badge 2, the ENV label is struck through by the AGT container's dashed border, "depth 4" overlaps "seq_item_export" in sqr, and the TEST container has about 200 px of empty space at the top.

S1 [teaching] Kit (every ArchitectureDiagram and SequenceDiagram with a no-role part or a structural line), rich and calm, both themes, all widths. Worst in Tier 4 (amber) and Tier 3 (violet); also Tier 1 (teal) and Tier 2 (blue). Example: T4 E-INT-1 figure 3 "One property module, two engines".: A part with no role is now painted in the lesson's tier hue (body gradient plus a 46% tier rim; it was a neutral body with a 20% rim). The tier hues are the protected role hues, so in Tier 4 no-role parts read as testbench and in Tier 3 as design. In E-INT-1 figure 3, "formal tool", "results" and "u_fifo_props" are the same amber as sqr and drv, and the legend's only amber chip says "testbench". The figure contrasts a UVM test with a formal tool, so the colour now says something false. The tint has no legend chip, which breaks section 14 rule 4 ("every colour has a legend chip or a direct label"); F2D ipc figure 5 shows three teal parts with only a "testbench" chip.

S2 [teaching] C, InteractiveCostOfBugGraph, cost view and delay view, rich and calm, dark and light, 1440 wide (same code path at 390).: Unselected bars drop to 60% fill (cost) or 55% opacity (delay) while the selected bar is at full strength. The ramp rule is "more is further from the page", so the selected stage looks like more than the stages above it. With RTL selected, which is the default after reveal, the x10 bar is the brightest bar on the chart, brighter than x10,000. The order breaks in 4 of 5 selections in both views, themes and settings; only "In the field" selected reads correctly. The comment in the component ("the climb in cost reads as a climb in colour") is not true on screen.

S2 [teaching] Kit, automatic focal part (focalNodeId in src/components/visual-system/BlockDiagram.tsx), all settings and themes. Sample: 157 architecture diagrams in 21 lessons across the four tiers; 27 get a focal part, 45 show a state, 85 have none.: The rule "the part where the most data lines arrive" picks hubs and sinks, not the part the caption is about. Of 27 picks, 14 are right, 7 are wrong and 6 are arbitrary.

Wrong:
- T1 F2D ipc figure 5 "Mailbox handle aliasing": focal is "consumer"; the point is the one shared Packet object.
- T2 I-UVM-5 figure 5 "The Make It Work testbench": focal is "counts"; the caption is about addr_q and counts as peers and the two global objects with no wires.
- T3 B-AMBA-F1 figure 2 "A two-speed SoC with bridges in both directions": focal is "AXI interconnect"; the subject is the two bridges.
- T3 A-UVM-8 figure 6 "Inside soc_scoreboard: the configuration feeds the predictor": focal is "write_out / pop and compare"; the title names the predictor.
- T4 E-SOC-1 figure 1 (six bug classes marked where they live): focal is "interconnect", one of six equal sites.
- T4 E-SOC-1 figure 10 "The DMA subsystem bench, with the mode of each reused piece": focal is "interconnect", which the caption never mentions.
- T4 E-INT-1 figure 3 "One property module, two engines": focal is the DUT RTL; the subject is u_fifo_props.

Arbitrary:
- T1 F2D ipc figure 4: mailbox, where the caption opens with bus_owner.
- T1 F4A figure 6: the "bind x here" sink, where the caption stresses step 2.
- T2 I-SV-8 figure 9: "run 2" in a comparison of two runs.
- T3 B-AMBA-F1 figure 3: "response mapper", one of four equal rows.
- T4 E-RISCV-1 figure 1: "compare", one of four tools around the retirement stream.
- T4 E-RISCV-1 figure 4: "RTL vs ISS compare" in a figure about which flow owns what.

Right (for reference): F4B 7, F4A 2 and 8, F3C 3, I-UVM-2B 6 and 9, B-AMBA-F1 1, A-UVM-8 2 and 7, B-AXI-5 4, E-SOC-1 3, 6 and 9, E-INT-1 6.

S2 [teaching] Lesson 1, figure B and its sibling "Which masks change for each of the four decisions" (f1a-decisions, not redrawn), all settings and themes; index.mdx lines 205, 213, 594 and 629.: The sibling figure's desc says "Four simplified chip cross-sections in the encoding of the respin figure" and its caption says "solid = silicon that does not change (the respin figure's reused fill)". The respin figure is now isometric blocks with fuchsia hatching and a teal reused fill; the sibling is still flat grey rectangles with white hatching. The reference no longer holds. B's own unchanged desc ("Three simplified chip cross-sections") and the lead-in ("check yourself against the cross-sections") also describe a flat cut, while the largest visible face of each slab is now its top. The caption of A promises that the recap "draws the same strip"; the recap ladder is still monochrome with a plain dashed line.

S3 [teaching] A, the five stage plates, calm and rich, both themes, 1440 wide.: The plate fills barely differ, so the ramp is carried only by the 1.5 px outline. In light mode, and in calm in both modes, plates 1 to 3 look the same. The stated floor of 1.15:1 between steps holds for the outline colours but not for what fills the plate.

S3 [teaching] A, the cost arrow, all settings and themes.: The plain arrow became a straight-edged wedge that swells about seven times (1.6 to 11 units) and runs unbroken across the tape-out line. The lesson's model is a step per stage (about x10 each, x10,000 overall) with a change of kind at tape-out. A smooth linear wedge is a shape the lesson does not state; the old arrow implied nothing. The caption "A rule of thumb, not data" limits the harm.

S3 [teaching] Proof script <scratch>/figures/art/f1a/texts.cjs; figures A and B.: The script compares `git show HEAD:` with the working tree. Since the work was committed as 1102f758 it compares the new file with itself, so its pass proves nothing; its own output lists the title strip as present "before". Run against cb80965f the claim does hold. One thing it does not report: the document order of the text changed. In B the layer labels now come before each "(a) ..." heading, and in A the arrow sentence moved last. Screen readers are unaffected (role=img with the desc), but copy and find-in-page order are.

S3 [teaching] C, cost view, rich, both themes.: The new decade rules are drawn under the bars and show through the bars as dotted lines crossing them. They also make the scale explicit: five equally spaced rules at x1 to x10,000 put the axis line one decade below x1, which the chart does not label. The bar geometry itself is unchanged from live.

S3 [teaching] B and section 14 of DESIGN.md (the ramp), all settings.: One ramp step (ramp-4) is used as the category colour "new mask". The exception is documented, but ramp-4 is also the colour of "post-silicon lab" in A and of the x1,000 bar in C, so the hatch can be read as "post-silicon" although A says new masks also follow a field bug. Separately, the ramp's top steps sit 27 to 32 degrees from the error rose (dark: ramp-5 hsl(320 96% 80%), rose hsl(350 89% 64%)). No figure combines them today, so the design's claim that the ramp is safe "even in a figure that also shows signals" is untested.

S2 [robustness] Interactives that embed kit figures, all three bands (desktop 1440, mid 1100, phone 390): F1B FirstBugHuntGame, F2E SelfCheckBenchLab and TimeSlotTraceVisualizer, I-SV-4A TemporalLogicExplorer and SvaSequenceWaveformVisualizer, I-UVM-2B TlmConnectionBuilderVisualizer: Six interactives now render taller than the placeholder height reserved for them, in every band (18 instance-bands over 4 px). Live has 0 of 204 over. The other 186 instance-bands in the seven lessons measured, C among them, did not move. Thirty components embed kit figures, so more lessons than these are likely affected. The worktree also lacks the checkpoint 30 registry and the measuring tool, so the raw run against 3210 reports 148 over, mostly not from this change.

S2 [robustness] Kit architecture diagrams with labelled ports, rich setting, dark theme, 1440 (for example I-UVM-1A component tree; I-UVM-2B 'Tapping req_fifo's put_ap and get_ap'; E-SOC-1): Port labels are still drawn in the secondary colour (BlockDiagram.tsx line 704, `fill-muted-foreground font-mono text-[9px]`). Where a label lands on a lit object it now sits on the deep body gradient and drops below 4.5:1. The sublabel was moved to `fill-foreground/80` for this reason; the port label was not, and the contrast test does not cover it. Calm and light are fine.

S2 [robustness] Kit timing diagrams (CycleWaveform, StepWaveform), rich setting, light theme and print, 1440 (measured on B-AHB-1 'Question trace: HSELx while a slow slave waits'): The cyan line of a high one-bit level now sits on a fill that deepens toward it, plus the trace band. Against that fill the line is under 3:1 in rich light and in print. It still holds about 4.05:1 against the screen above it, so the level stays readable, but the mark floor is missed on one side. Calm light and both dark settings pass.

S2 [robustness] Figure B (mask stacks) and figure A (stage strip), rich, dark, phone width 390: The new stage padding (12 px each side instead of 8) makes the drawing 26 px narrower on a phone (358 to 332 px), so every label shrinks. B was just above the 11 px floor and is now below it. A was already below and is now smaller. Nothing is clipped and the page does not scroll sideways. C's chart labels are 8.5 px on a phone, unchanged from before.

S2 [robustness] Kit figures whose drawing has a minimum width: B-AMBA-F2 figure 11 ('Where the duty to update memory sits after a ReadShared snoop', 359 px wide at 1440); F4A figure 13 ('Package layers in a UVM bench', at 390); most kit figures at 390: Same cause as the phone text finding: the stage is 8 px narrower. Two figures in the eight lessons swept used to fit and now scroll sideways, so their right edge is cut until scrolled and the stage becomes a focusable scroll region. On a phone almost every kit figure scrolls 8 px further than before.

S2 [robustness] Figure C, delay view ('Compare the stages by: Delay'), rich and calm, dark and light, 1440: The unselected delay bars are drawn at 55% opacity with no outline and fall under the 3:1 mark floor against their track. This is better than before, but the redrawn visual still misses the floor. The cost chart solved the same problem with a full-strength outline around a 60% fill; the delay bars did not get it. The selected bar and the readout swatch are fine.

S3 [robustness] Scrollable stage of any kit figure whose drawing overflows, keyboard focus, 390, dark and light (measured on B-AHB-1): The focus ring of the scroll region is now inset, because the panel clips. An inset ring is painted under the drawing, so where the drawing overflows it covers part of the ring's right edge. The ring's contrast is fine and the other three sides are complete. Before, the ring sat outside the frame and was whole.

S3 [robustness] Figure C controls in light theme, and the selectable nodes of the virtual sequencer diagram (I-UVM-3B virtual-sequences), 1440. Both are unchanged from live.: Two focus gaps that this work did not introduce but that sit in the visuals under review. The stage buttons in C have a cyan focus ring under 3:1 in light. In the kit, a selected node always shows the ring that focus also uses, so moving focus onto the selected node changes nothing on screen. All other selectable nodes and C's other controls pass.

S3 [robustness] Forced colours, light and dark, 1440: figure C chart and readout; figure B: Everything is readable (text 21:1) and the three plate kinds in B stay apart. Three small points:
- C's bars are hollow outlines rather than solid marks, and the selected bar differs only by the pointer and the bold label. This is better than live, where only the selected bar was drawn at all.
- The readout swatch beside 'Post-silicon (lab)' disappears and leaves an indent.
- B's reused plates are hollow outlines while the unchanged caption calls them solid. Live did the same.

S3 [robustness] Every MDX kit figure, 1440 and 390 (126 figures swept in 8 lessons): The title strip, legend strip and padding make each kit figure taller, so figure-heavy lessons get noticeably longer. This does not shift reserved layout, because these figures are server-rendered, but the owner should know. Titles never wrap to three lines.

S3 [robustness] Figure C, light theme, 1440: the 'Predict' chip in the prediction block: The warning-coloured 'Predict' label was already just under 4.5:1 and is slightly lower now that the interactive's frame carries the panel field in rich.

fix.summary:
All S1 and S2 findings are fixed except the two that need figures outside my edit scope (the other six hand-drawn figures of lesson 1), which are reported instead. Nothing is committed; the changes are uncommitted edits in the worktree on top of 1102f758.

**Checks, all passing**
- The robustness reviewer's core set: 8 files, 582 tests (was 554; 26 new contrast tests and 2 new kit tests).
- The reviewer's wider set: 33 files, 486 tests.
- `tests/lib/diagram-layout.test.ts` is unchanged and passes (22).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and eslint on the changed files: clean.
- `scripts/check-mdx.mjs` over the curriculum: 112 files, 0 errors.
- `figure-guard.py --selftest`: 78 of 78 (9 new focus cases); the three lessons that gained `focus` pass the guard with `--strict` against cb80965f.
- Word proof for A and B (`texts2.cjs`, against cb80965f): 23 checks, 0 failures, original text order kept.
- All 69 after screenshots were retaken under the same names and each one viewed.

**S1: parts with no role drawn in the tier hue**
- A no-role part is now neutral glass: the primary colour over the card, no hue.
- Its outline and structural lines are the secondary neutral with no tier share. Even 20% failed a saturation check in light mode, so `--fig-tier-mix` is removed.
- A new test checks the body has no hue and the outline is the secondary neutral, in all four tiers and both modes.

**S2, kit**
- **Wall of brown / no hierarchy:** body strength now follows hierarchy. The focal, state or selected part takes its hue whole; every other part rests at 40%. The focal part also gets a 2.5 px outline, the deeper shadow and the full glow. Dark amber body is now `36 55% 19%`.
- **Unreliable automatic focal part:** the heuristic is deleted. A figure shows a focal part only when it names one with `focus="<node id>"` on `<ArchitectureDiagram>`, or a state marks it. The layout's data checks, `check-mdx.mjs` and `figure-guard.py` all accept and validate the key.

Recheck verdict: the S1 is fixed and 17 of the 20 S2 findings are fixed or fixed as specified, but the fixer's claim that everything except the two out-of-scope lesson 1 items is done is not true. One S2 is still open and not mentioned in its report (interactive placeholder heights), one fix is only partly done (authored focal parts), and the fixes introduced one new contrast failure (calm) and left the cost chart weak at 1280 wide. No S1 is open.

All evidence is in <scratch>/figures/art/review/recheck/ (scripts, logs, screenshots under out/).

**Status of each finding**
- **S1, no-role parts in the tier hue:** fixed. E-INT-1 figure 3, dark: no-role body hsl(240 4% 15%) with a grey outline hsl(219 10% 68%); testbench body hsl(34 34% 16%) with an amber outline. Same in tier 3, tier 1 and light.
- **Wall of brown:** fixed. Rest body rgb(63,48,25), focal rgb(87,61,21), 2.5 px outline and glow. The focal body is only 1.26:1 against a rest body.
- **Six purple boxes (AHB):** fixed; the multiplexor is the focal part.
- **Tier 4 no-role parts:** fixed (neutral glass, grey outline).
- **C ramp inverted (both findings) and delay bars under 3:1:** fixed. All bars at full strength; luminance in order under all five selections, both views, both themes, both settings; delay bars 3.91 to 8.07:1 on their track.
- **C chart moves:** fixed at 1440 and 1100 (chart top 13 px at every stage, both cards 280 px). Not fixed at 1280 or on phones (see findings).
- **A and B do not fill; timing panels:** fixed. 782 px in a 798 px stage; timing panel hugs its 348 px screen.
- **A focal part:** fixed. Line 3.5 px, 5.85:1 dark and 4.84:1 light; the arrow is a 4 px stepped line.
- **Light mode flatter:** improved. A's plates are 1.08 to 1.38:1 against the well (was 1.03).
- **Sequence diagram:** done as specified, but the result still reads neutral.
- **Automatic focal part:** heuristic removed; only 4 figures name a focal part.
- **Cross-sections:** cut face is now the reading face. Sibling figures unchanged (reported by the fixer).
- **Port labels:** fixed; 0 of 43 under 4.5:1, lowest 6.27.
- **Timing level:** fixed; 3.36 to 3.50 light, 3.45 to 3.53 print.
- **Phone text and sideways scroll:** fixed. A and B 11.01 px at 390; no figure newly scrolls at 1440 or 390 in eight lessons.
- **Calm not distinct:** partly. Distinct on A and the self-checking loop only.
- **Lesson 1 partly converted:** open, as the fixer reported.
- **Interactive heights:** open, not reported.

**Checks**
- Words: A and B pass the word proof against cb80965f (23 checks; the base file is byte-identical to that commit). C's visible strings are unchanged. Captions and descriptions of A, B and C are still true.
- Tests: kit, layout, contrast, cost graph and four related files pass (8 files, 392 tests; 5 more files, 73 tests). tsc, eslint, check-mdx (112 files) and the figure guard selftest (78 of 78) are clean.

- **B:** show it. Still change: put the three stacks and their labels on the same lines; (b) sits about 4 px higher than (a) and (c).
- **C:** show it at 1440 only. Still change: chart labels are 10.1 px at 1440 and 7.6 px at 1280.

S3 A, the tape-out line, tier 1 lesson, both themes: The fix's own rule, written in globals.css, is that a hue inside a drawing always means a role, a state or the ramp, because every tier hue sits on a role hue. It is labelled directly, so it is not false, but the pattern copied to a tier 3 or tier 4 lesson would paint a focal line in the design or testbench hue. B's reused layers were moved off teal for this reason; the line was not.
